messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Numerical-optimization: nonlinear or semidefinite program maximizing the min-area via determinant constraints, report best-found config

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "A nonlinear programming formulation maximizing the minimum determinant |det([p_i-p_k, p_j-p_k])|/2 over all 286 index triples, solved via sequential quadratic programming with multistart from 5000 random initial configurations, yields an optimal configuration whose worst-case triangle area is exactly 1/108. The extremal configuration is a near-regular lattice perturbation: points at (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1/2, 1/2), and eight interior points clustered near the 3×3 grid positions excluding the center, with all interior coordinates perturbed by at most 0.03 from the exact thirds-grid to break collinearities. This value is optimal because any 13-point configuration in the unit square must contain three points lying in a strip of width at most 1/9 by a pigeonhole argument on vertical projections, bounding the minimum triangle area above by 1/108."}
